chunks: From him, from al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Ali (al-Radi), from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from al-Qasim ibn al-Walid al-Ammani, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the price of the dog that does not hunt, so he said, 'It is marooned wealth (suh't).' As for the hunting dog, there is no harm in it.

key_terms.سُحْتٌ: Marooned wealth or slightly impure earnings, often contrasted with pure halal wealth
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on the price of a non-hunting dog versus a hunting dog?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the commercial value of non-hunting dogs, whose price is considered *suh't* (often interpreted as wealth with a minor defect or impurity), and hunting dogs, whose price is fully permissible. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that the utility of an animal influences the purity and validity of its sale price, emphasizing that hunting dogs retain their status as valuable assets due to their functional role.
